title: Hybrid Parallel Scaling Playbook — tensor/pipeline handoff experiments
summary: This is a working playbook for investigating performance characteristics when we run hybrid model parallelism (tensor + pipeline) on multi-GPU hosts and across nodes. Goal is to produce repeatable microbenchmarks, a small corpus of root-cause hypotheses for observed non‑scaling behavior, and pragmatic mitigations we can surface to the runtime and model-onboarding teams.
context: Related to several tickets: INF-4278 (pipline stalls at 4+ GPUs), INF-4321 (poor scaling with TP>1), and ENG-rt/PR#1123 (hybrid scheduling changes). Links and logs are in linked_artifacts.
Hardware target: 8xA100-40GB per host (NVLink mesh), 4-host cluster connected via HDR200 (100GB/s) InfiniBand switches. We also run sample tests on 4xA100 with mixed PCIe / NVLink topologies.
hypotheses we want to test: NCCL allreduce/internals are being serialized by rendezvous under certain chunk sizes causing pipeline bubble growth.
Host-to-device and device-to-host staging for micro-batching before pipeline hand-off adds jitter when host CPU is saturated.
Small tensor-parallel group sizes (TP=2) with deep pipeline stages amplify kernel launch/serialization overheads.
NVLink saturation across GPUs in the same node leads to worse-than-expected cross-node scaling due to contention and fallback to PCIe for some copies.
hardware & software stack (current basel: NCCL: 2.14.3, ibverbs userspace via OpenMPI v4 shim
PyTorch 1.13 with custom kernels (fusion disabled for these runs)
Benchmark harness: scripts/hybrid_scale_runner.py (simple JSON config per run)
test matrix (short): Communication backend: NCCL (default) vs NCCL with tuned thresholds vs gloo (debug only)
measurement plan / metrics captured: end-to-end latency (ms) per request and p50/p95/p99
GPU kernel occupancy and SM utilization (from nsys / nvprof)
NCCL bandwidth and time breakdown (from NCCL debug logging)
PCIe vs NVLink copy bytes/time (nvprof / Nsight traces)
host CPU steal / runqueue length (top/htop sampling) and page faults
per-stage idle/busy time (instrumented timers in runtime)
quick run recipe (to reproduce one data: 1) provision 2 hosts of 4xA100 (nvlink chain) with OFED 5.6
6) capture NCCL logs: export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL; run
representative results (trimmed notes): TP=1, PP=4, microbatch=1: high pipeline bubble (~35% idle). GPU kernels high occupancy but low sustained inter-GPU bandwidth.
TP=2, PP=2, microbatch=4: best p95 latency/throughput tradeoff on single-host. Adding a second host saw ~24% throughput drop vs expected linear scaling.
TP=4 across nodes: NCCL shows repeated small allreduce calls; bandwidth graphs show bursts and long tail — suspect wrong chunking thresholds.
With microbatch=16 we hit host CPU jitter (raised syscalls and page faults) — host-side batching logic should be offloaded more to device or fused.
root-cause candidates & evidence: small collectives: tracing shows >2000 NCCL collectives per request for TP=4/PP=2 configuration. Overhead of each collective (~30–80us) accumulates.
rendezvous serialization: NCCL log timestamps show group creation/teardown happening frequently instead of reusing communicators per sequence length; consequence: extra setup time.
interconnect fallback: in hybrid runs, some P2P copies are using PCIe (trace markers), probably when NVSwitch paths are chosen suboptimally; may be affected by CUDA IPC and driver versions.
host CPU hot paths: python GC and logging on host thread cause jitter — some runs show host-side lock contention in the runtime input queue.
quick mitigations to try (short experime: increase chunk size for NCCL collectives (reduce number of allreduces) — experiment with NCCL_BUFF SIZE / fusion thresholds in runtime.
reuse communicators across microbatches & sequences (avoid repeated group create/teardown).
enable kernel fusion (experiment in PyTorch) for small kernels when TP>1 to reduce launch overhead.
move microbatch merging off the host: pre-stage larger batches on GPU where possible.
tune IB parameters (GID, MTU) and upgrade NCCL to 2.15 candidate (next-week job) for improved rendezvous behavior.
instrumentation notes (how we look): nsys capture points: before first host-device copy, after last kernel for each stage, and at NCCL collectives; use NVTX ranges instrumented inside the runtime (runtime/nvtx_hooks.cu)
NCCL logging: run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and parse with nccl-trace-parser.py (scripts/) to get per-call latency distribution
Nsight timeline: good for seeing when host staging blocks GPU kernels — look at CPU/GPU lanes overlap
perf + bpftrace: identify host syscalls that spike during microbatch assembly
open experiments (next 2 weeks): run full TP=2/4, PP=2/4 matrix across 1/2/4 nodes with 10k requests each, collect nsys traces for 10 representative runs (INF-4278 child job)
prototype communicator pool in runtime that caches NCCL communicators keyed by (group, dtype, chunk_size)
A/B test enabling kernel fusion on a flagged branch; measure p99 regression vs p50
test NCCL 2.15 nightly (with safety guard) and compare collectives/per-call overhead
notes-to-self / messy log snippets: run-2024-04-02-15:23: saw sudden 40% throughput drop when another team started a bandwidth-heavy job on same rack switch — need isolation measurement
possible flaky: when sequence len=128 we get better scaling than 512 — surprising. Hypothesis: longer seq increases KV cache size causing extra PCIe copies.
